readme: Synthetic, independently authored extension for the ten October stories. Frozen before reranker evaluation; no original match-104 case or accepted label is modified. This file is development and release coverage evidence, not a protected or blind holdout. Ages 6 in the Keller slice are hermetic diagnostics and cannot enter the adult public intake. Each hard label expresses a specific documented distinction; failed shortlist survival remains a failure. Do not widen accepted labels, keyword routes, historical age ranges, top-K, or thresholds to make these cases pass.

cases.feeling: I have spent years preparing to do something useful, but I am afraid to tell a friend the unfinished plan. I don't know how to begin.
cases.note: Fear of speaking an existing useful plan and needing a collaborator, rather than discovering a vocation through an activity.

cases.feeling: I keep studying and preparing instead of beginning the work I say matters. I want to talk it through with someone, but I doubt the plan will sound real.
cases.note: Preparation delaying a concrete plan and fear of sharing it; no invented clinical condition or lifelong aimlessness.

cases.feeling: I am the only woman in my training class. A difficult practical lesson left me shaken, and they don't think I belong there. I still want a chance to learn beside them.
cases.note: Attending and returning to a difficult clinical class, rather than leaving to find a flight school abroad.

cases.feeling: The material in a class I fought to enter makes my heart pound. I need to get through the next lesson without pretending it is easy.
cases.note: Documented bodily strain during a dissection and continued learning; not a claim of a panic diagnosis.

cases.feeling: I want to take an opportunity to work away from home, but my family thinks I should stay with the safe profession they planned. I already declined and now I am reconsidering.
cases.note: A specific offer and family objections to a working trip, rather than women being legally excluded from university study.

cases.feeling: My father disapproves of the work I want to try. Someone else in the family understands it, but I still don't know if I am prepared to leave.
cases.note: Attested family objection, relative's help and unsettled preparation; no invented rejection by a university.

cases.feeling: I have worked and saved toward the freedom someone promised me. Now that I can meet the terms, the person controlling my life wants to refuse. I feel trapped again.
cases.note: Negotiating a promised release after accumulating the agreed payment, rather than identity and employment after escape.

cases.feeling: I keep earning money so I can stop being under someone else's control. A promised payment failed, and I need another way to get what I was told would make me free.
cases.note: Failed expected payment followed by continued earnings; does not claim the failed payment was the only route.

cases.feeling: Illness made it hard to keep my business going. I have people depending on me, and now I may have to ask my family for a place to work.
cases.note: Illness, practical income failure and a family shop, rather than dissatisfaction with an aimless life.

cases.feeling: I got sick and couldn't do the work my small business needed. Several jobs have not worked out. I need wages for my family even if the next job is ordinary.
cases.note: Illness and dependent-family income pressure; no invented disgrace, alcohol diagnosis or dramatic comeback.

cases.feeling: I am hiding from the person who controlled me. My children are nearby, but I cannot go to them or let them hear me. I am waiting for a way to leave safely.
cases.note: Confinement and separation while still pursued, rather than adjusting to a new identity after reaching safety.

cases.feeling: I escaped into hiding, but I am still trapped in one small place. I can hear my family outside and cannot answer. Staying out of sight is wearing down my body.
cases.note: Prolonged concealment with nearby family and bodily costs; no suggestion that legal freedom follows immediately.

cases.feeling: I worked without receiving the wages I was promised. I am hungry and think my efforts have been wasted. A former teacher may be able to introduce me for one paid trial.
cases.note: Unpaid employment and an introduced paid reporting trial, rather than poverty during travel toward school.

cases.feeling: I have tried selling and writing, but I am broke and have no hope left. I can try one more introduction for work, although it will not pay me until I prove I can do it.
cases.note: Attested despair and reporting trial after unpaid labor and unsuccessful sales; no invented artistic dream.

cases.feeling: I have experience caring for sick people, but every offer to help is dismissed. I think who I am may be part of it. I still want to serve and may have to pay my own way.
cases.note: Exclusion from official nursing service despite experience and an independent costly route, rather than illness after accepted wartime service.

cases.feeling: They won't accept my offer to care for people, even with references. I cried after the refusals. I could go independently, but I have limited money and no guaranteed welcome.
cases.note: Rejected offers, attested tears and financially limited independent travel; racial motivation remains the figure's suspicion.

cases.feeling: I left home to get an education, but I ran out of money for food or a room. I am looking for work so I can reach the school and ask for a chance.
cases.note: Material obstacles on a trip toward school, rather than an unpaid newspaper job and a introduced reporting trial. Age 18 respects public intake; the historical range stays 16–17.

cases.feeling: I reached a school hungry and with hardly any money. Other students are being accepted while I wait. If they give me a practical task, I want to do it carefully.
cases.note: Waiting for admission and a cleaning task; adult analogy rather than an invented change to historical age.

cases.feeling: I am angry when my teacher takes away the toy I want. I cannot make her understand me, and I am learning another way to tell her what I need.
cases.note: Hermetic under-18 diagnostic only: a child's communication lesson, rather than the later teacher's own education and eye treatment.

cases.feeling: I have a disability and cannot use speech to ask for things. Someone is helping me learn signs, but getting my meaning across is still difficult.
cases.note: Hermetic under-18 diagnostic only. Does not assert a disability cure or iconic sudden recognition; cannot be submitted through the adult public intake.
